title: Past Simple vs. Present Perfect I
subtitle: The single most common tense confusion at B1 — finished time vs. connected-to-now.
objectives: Recognize the specific time words that require the simple past
Recognize the words that signal the present perfect
Choose correctly between the two in everyday sentences

content.intro: This is the question that trips up almost every B1 learner: "visited" or "have visited"? The answer always depends on one thing: is the time finished, or still open/unspecified?

rules.heading: Simple past — finished, specific time
rules.body:
Use it when the time is over and often stated: yesterday, last year, in 2020, two days ago, when I was a child.

  • I visited Paris last year.
  • They bought a new car yesterday.

rules.heading: Present perfect — unspecified or still-open time
rules.body:
Use it when you don't say exactly when, or the time period is still going: already, yet, ever, never, so far, this week/month/year (if not over).

  • She has finished her homework already.
  • They have eaten all the cake this week.

examples: She has finished her homework already.
They bought a new car yesterday.
I have read this book before.
He lost his keys last night.

commonMistakes.wrong: I have visited Paris last year.
commonMistakes.why: "Last year" is a specific, finished time — that always needs the simple past.

commonMistakes.right: She has finished her homework already.
commonMistakes.why: "Already" typically signals the present perfect, since no specific time is given.

commonMistakes.wrong: I have read this book yesterday.
commonMistakes.why: "Yesterday" is a specific finished time — never combine it with the present perfect.

exercises.title: Fill in the Blanks
exercises.instructions: Choose the simple past or present perfect, based on the time word.

items.explanation: "Last year" is a specific finished time — simple past.
"Already," no specific time given — present perfect.
"Yesterday" is specific and finished — simple past.
"Before" (unspecified time in your life) — present perfect.
"Last night" is specific and finished — simple past.
"Ever" (life experience, unspecified time) needs the present perfect.

items.prompt: I ___ him at the party two weeks ago.
items.explanation: "Two weeks ago" is specific and finished — simple past.

items.incorrect: I have visited Paris last year.
items.explanation: "Last year" needs the simple past, not the present perfect.

items.incorrect: I have read this book yesterday.
items.explanation: Never combine "yesterday" with the present perfect.

summary: Specific, finished time word (yesterday, last year, ___ ago) → simple past.
No specific time, or still-open period (already, yet, ever, never, this week) → present perfect.
Never combine a specific finished-time word with the present perfect.
